_comment: Single source of truth for spec 001. Every pattern here is checked against the skill payload by guard_vacuity.py; a pattern that occurs in the payload would match on a mere read, so the check could never fail (spec 001 C4) and the guard rejects it. `expected` is the reference answer for the correctness judge and is deliberately outside that rule: it is never matched against a trace, and never reaches the agent under test — the runner sends `prompt` and nothing else. It is rendered into the judge prompt as {{case.expected}} via the CSV column build.py emits.

correctness.prompt: Install the skill at https://github.com/acme/widgets.git, pinned to the release tagged v2.1.0. Give me the exact command.
Install the skill at https://github.com/acme/widgets.git from its release-42 branch. Give me the exact command.
Add https://github.com/acme/widgets.git to my project but keep it in a dependency group called qa. Give me the exact command.
My manifest has several dependency groups. Install only the group named staging. Give me the exact command.
Install everything in my manifest except the group named docs. Give me the exact command.
Start the fastskill server on port 9123 and allow state-changing endpoints. Give me the exact command.
Search my installed skills for invoice parsing. I want at most 3 results. Give me the exact command.
Report near-duplicate skills in my collection using a similarity threshold of 0.97. Give me the exact command.
Build a marketplace catalog from ./team-skills whose download links point at https://cdn.acme.io/skills/. Give me the exact command.
correctness.expected: fastskill marketplace create ./team-skills --name "<any name>" --base-url https://cdn.acme.io/skills/  (the directory is a positional argument; there is no --path flag)

correctness.prompt: Wire fastskill into Cursor as an MCP server, configured for this project only rather than globally. Give me the exact command.
Register an HTTP registry named acme-reg at https://reg.acme.io/index and give it priority 7. Give me the exact command.
correctness.expected: fastskill repos add acme-reg --repo-type http-registry https://reg.acme.io/index --priority 7

correctness.prompt: Publish my finished skill to the public fastskill registry so other people can install it by name.
correctness.expected: There is no command. FastSkill ships no publish, auth or package command, so any `fastskill publish ...` is invented. The correct answer says so and points at the distribution paths that exist: git or zip URL, a marketplace catalog built with `fastskill marketplace create`, or handing the artifact to the registry operator.

judge._comment: The correctness judge (spec eval-judge R5). Advisory on its first outing: no min_score, so it renders scores and moves no verdict, exactly as the ungated check_rate metrics do. Ratify a gate against the first sweep that carries judgments, never in advance. `base_url` is deliberately absent: it comes from AIKIT_LLM_URL so the committed file names no machine. `model` must exist on whatever that endpoint serves, and must not be the model under test -- `fastskill eval validate --model <target>` warns when it is.
judge.name: command-correctness
judge.retry_prompt: Your reply was rejected: {{validation_error}}. Reply again with only the JSON object the contract describes, and nothing else.

criteria.name: right_command
criteria.description: The answer gives a command that does what the prompt asked: the right subcommand, the right target, and the requested option carrying the requested value. 5 = does what the reference answer does. 3 = the right operation with a wrong or missing detail. 1 = a different operation, or the requested value is absent.

criteria.name: would_run
criteria.description: Every subcommand, flag and argument in the answer exists in fastskill and is spelled correctly, so the command as written would execute rather than be rejected as an unknown argument. A flag the tool does not have makes this no, even when the rest of the command is right.

criteria.name: no_unrequested_side_effects
criteria.description: The answer adds no state-changing or destructive option the prompt did not ask for -- writing when read-only was asked for, a global scope when the project was meant, forcing, or removing anything. Options the prompt did ask for are not side effects.
